source.author: verg
source.text: omnigenumque deum monstra et latrator Anubis contra Neptunum et Venerem contraque Minervam tela tenent.
source.text_original: omnigenumque deum monstra et latrator Anubis / contra Neptunum et Venerem contraque Minervam / tela tenent.
source.text_english: and monsters of every kind of gods and barking Anubis hold their weapons against Neptune and Venus and against Minerva.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Unde et Virgilius ait: Omnigenumque deum monstra, et latrator Anubis, Quasi non et illa sint monstra quae laudat Contra Neptunum et Venerem, contraque Minervam.
reuse.text_original: Unde et Virgilius ait: Omnigenumque deum monstra, et latrator Anubis, Quasi non et illa sint monstra quae laudat Contra Neptunum et Venerem, contraque Minervam.
reuse.text_english: Hence Virgil also says: and the monsters of every kind of gods, and barking Anubis, as though those too were not monsters which he praises against Neptune and Venus and against Minerva.
